_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401909966.text: Both teams arrive frustrated. Washington have lost four straight, and Anthony Davis scored 44 in his return and then said flatly that the team is "not playing any defense". Indiana are 0-4 at home and have lost seven of eight with Tyrese Haliburton out indefinitely, and Rick Carlisle came out of Monday's last-second loss in Dallas ripping the officials. Neither side has a clear mental edge. Davis's visible frustration could cut either way; a slight lean goes to Indiana's desperation to win a first home game.

401909967.text: This is a rematch four days after New York won 109-97 in Cleveland, the Knicks' fifth straight win over the Cavs. Marc Stein reports Kenny Atkinson's seat is warming after Cleveland lost four of five, including at a short-handed Charlotte, so expect an urgent response. The Knicks are on a back-to-back with Josh Hart doubtful, and Karl-Anthony Towns' stalled extension talks are a background distraction. On mood the lean is toward Cleveland's urgency, but the Knicks' recent dominance in this matchup is real.

401909968.text: Boston come in buoyant after a 123-101 rout in Philadelphia, where Paul George scored 36 against his former team, though they are on the second night of a back-to-back. Toronto are running thin: Scottie Barnes (groin) misses a third straight game, Kawhi Leonard is out at least another week, and Quickley is questionable. Toronto also face Philadelphia tomorrow. Confidence and health both lean toward Boston.

401909969.text: San Antonio bring the league's longest winning streak (nine) to Chicago, fresh off Victor Wembanyama's 40-point, nine-block night in Phoenix. There is a homecoming subplot: Billy Donovan, Chicago's coach for six seasons until last spring, returns as a Spurs assistant. Chicago have lost seven straight and have allowed 124 or more in nine in a row. The Spurs' momentum is the dominant mental factor; the only counterweight is the usual risk of a big favourite relaxing.

401909970.text: Denver's travel was messy: travel delays after Saturday's Mexico City game got them back only hours before Monday's loss in Houston. They have had a day to reset since. Memphis have the league's second-youngest roster and are 5-0 on the road but have lost three straight at home. A tired Denver and a young team uneasy at home roughly cancel out, with a slight lean to Denver now that it has had rest.

401909971.text: Milwaukee are 1-10, have lost seven straight, and are one loss from tying the worst start in franchise history. Taylor Jenkins admits "what we're doing right now is not working", and Kyle Kuzma, facing the team where he started his career, has called for more urgency. Tyler Herro (knee) is out again, and the Bucks are on a back-to-back after a 32-point loss to the Knicks. The Lakers are on a six-game winning streak behind Luka Doncic. Everything mental leans toward Los Angeles.

401909972.text: Both teams are coming off embarrassments. New Orleans lost by 51 at Golden State, the worst regular-season loss in franchise history, and Jamahl Mosley said bluntly they got their "tail kicked". Brooklyn are rebuilding at 2-8 after a 37-point loss in Dallas, and Moritz Wagner questioned the team's maturity. Egor Demin is now probable after six missed games. The lean goes to a bounce-back from New Orleans at home with Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III back from rest, against a young team with little at stake.

401909974.text: Golden State have won eight straight after an 0-3 start, and Steve Kerr says the group is "having fun". That is despite Kristaps Porzingis stepping away for his health while the team withholds his salary and tries to trade him. This game opens a five-game road trip. Houston are thin up front, with Steven Adams and Clint Capela out, and Kevin Durant faces his former team while chasing Kobe Bryant on the all-time scoring list. The Warriors' chemistry is the strongest mental signal, so the lean is slightly toward Golden State.

401909976.text: Philadelphia return home after a 22-point loss to Boston in Jaylen Brown's first game against his old team, and should respond with focus. Toronto are on the second night of a back-to-back, have played two games without Scottie Barnes, and have Kawhi Leonard out at least another week. The bounce-back motivation and Toronto's fatigue and injuries both lean toward the 76ers.

401909977.text: This is a rematch three days after Detroit won 122-111 despite 44 points from Anthony Davis, who then criticised the Wizards' defense and rebounding in public. Washington reportedly want to see Davis play 20-30 games before deciding on an extension, so every night is a showcase. Detroit are without Jalen Duren (hamstring) for at least two more weeks. Davis's motivation is real, but a frustrated team on a long losing run is the weaker mental side; the lean stays with Detroit.

401909978.text: Minnesota have won four straight in the middle of an eight-game homestand, even without Anthony Edwards, who is out until late December after knee surgery. Dallas carry trade noise: Chris Mannix reports Kyrie Irving is "not on the Mavericks' timeline" and could be the deadline's biggest name, though others think Dallas keep him. Rumours like that can unsettle a team, but Irving has been producing. A slight lean to Minnesota's home rhythm.

401909979.text: Charlotte's injury list keeps growing: Dennis Schroder is out at least two weeks, Kon Knueppel at least four, and Brandon Miller has a hip strain. Charles Lee is reviewing the offseason routine while insisting there are "no excuses". Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale face Phoenix for the first time since the June trade that sent Miles Bridges to the Suns, so expect extra edge in that matchup. Phoenix are smarting from a 26-point loss in San Antonio and Jordan Ott's call for more support for Devin Booker. The lean goes to Phoenix.
